page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-128GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor using x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model, supported by 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU is present.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded compression and decompression (gzip and bzip3) ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Geekbench single-core scores are also strong, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is average, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores landing in the middle 50%. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while read-only memory bandwidth for small and large blocks is average, large-block write memory bandwidth and the PassMark memory score are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per core, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis (which achieved average performance in testing), and memory-heavy web serving. However, it is less optimal for large-scale LLM inference or write-heavy memory operations due to weaker large-block write bandwidth and lower multi-core scaling.
